question: A lab rates a dried chilli at 100,000 Scoville units. The fresh pod was 80% water. Its rating by fresh weight, in thousands?
move: Before comparing two concentrations, check that both divide by the same thing.
trap: Assuming drying changes nothing, since no capsaicin is lost.
hint: Drying removes water, not capsaicin: ask how much fresh pod holds one gram of dry matter.
steps: 100 g of fresh pod at 80% water holds 20 g of dry matter.
The same capsaicin is spread over 100 g fresh instead of 20 g dry: 5 times the mass.

diagram.caption: The same capsaicin spread over five times the mass: a fifth of the rating.

reference: Collins, Mayer Wasmund & Bosland, Improved method for quantifying capsaicinoids in Capsicum using high-performance liquid chromatography, HortScience, 1995
